place.en: the Near East and the Indus
place.pt: the Near East and the Indus

notYet: Not yet part of the Near East and the Indus

stages.name: Persian-held
stages.desc: Still under the Achaemenid king or his satraps and allied rajas

stages.name: Conquered
stages.desc: Taken by Alexander and held by his satraps and garrisons

stages.name: Army on the march
stages.desc: Alexander's army campaigns or marches through it that year

stages.name: Fleet's waters
stages.desc: The fleet sails its rivers or coast that year

stages.name: Phoenician base
stages.desc: Phoenician and Cypriot cities supplying ships, crews and timber

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: The Cypriot kings bring about 120 ships to Alexander at the siege of Tyre
Cypriot seamen in the army help crew the new fleet on the Hydaspes
Cypriot shipwrights and timber for the fleet gathering at Babylon

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Tyre falls after a seven-month siege; Sidon and Byblos put their fleets at Alexander's service
Phoenician sailors from the army crew the Indus fleet, thousands of kilometres east
Ships built in Phoenicia are taken apart and carried overland to the Euphrates

states.name: Syria
timeline: Damascus and the Phoenician island city of Arados submit to Alexander
The army marches inland and crosses the Euphrates at Thapsacus
Held by Macedonian governors on the road between the sea and Babylon
Phoenician warships are reassembled at Thapsacus and sail down the Euphrates

states.name: Iraq
timeline: Babylonia and Assyria, heartland of Darius III's empire
Alexander defeats Darius at Gaugamela and enters Babylon
Babylon is governed for Alexander by the Persian Mazaeus
Nearchus' fleet sails up the Tigris with Alexander to Opis
A harbour for a thousand warships is dug at Babylon for the Arabian expedition

states.name: Iran
timeline: Persis, Media and the royal capitals of the Achaemenid kings
Alexander takes Susa and forces the Persian Gates
Persepolis burns; Darius is murdered by his own satraps
The Iranian plateau is held by Alexander's satraps
The survivors of the Gedrosian desert regroup in Carmania
Nearchus sails up the Gulf and the Pasitigris river to Susa
Held by Alexander's satraps; Peucestas rules Persis

states.name: Pakistan
timeline: Gandhara and the Indus lands, Persian satrapies now ruled by Indian kings
Alexander fights his way down the Kabul and Swat valleys
Battle of the Hydaspes; in November the new fleet sets out down the river
The fleet reaches the Ocean; Nearchus sails west along the Makran coast
Indian satrapies under Peithon and the rajas Porus and Taxiles

states.name: Kuwait
timeline: Islands and shores at the head of the Persian Gulf
Alexander's scouts reach the island of Failaka, which he names Icarus

states.name: Afghanistan
timeline: Arachosia, Aria and Bactria, eastern satrapies of the Persian empire
The army marches through Aria, Drangiana and Arachosia
Alexander crosses the Hindu Kush into Bactria and hunts down Bessus
Hard war against the Bactrian and Sogdian revolt
Alexander marries Roxane and recrosses the Hindu Kush toward India
Bactria and Arachosia are held by garrisons and new Alexandrias
Craterus leads the veterans and elephants home through Arachosia
Held by Alexander's satraps and Greek settlers

events.title: Tyre falls
events.text: After a seven-month siege and a mole built across the strait, Alexander storms the island city of Tyre.

events.title: Kings of Cyprus
events.text: The kings of Salamis and the other Cypriot cities join Alexander with about 120 ships.

events.title: Sidon's fleet
events.text: Sidon, Byblos and Arados abandon Persia; their warships blockade Tyre for Alexander.

events.title: Siege of Gaza
events.text: Alexander takes Gaza after a two-month siege on his way to Egypt.

events.title: Crossing at Thapsacus
events.text: The army crosses the Euphrates on bridges of boats at Thapsacus.

events.title: Gaugamela
events.text: On 1 October Alexander routs Darius III's army east of the Tigris.

events.title: Babylon opens its gates
events.text: The satrap Mazaeus surrenders Babylon, which welcomes Alexander.

events.title: Susa
events.text: Alexander takes the Persian capital of Susa and its vast treasury.

events.title: Persian Gates
events.text: Alexander forces the mountain pass held by the satrap Ariobarzanes.

events.title: Persepolis burns
events.text: The palaces of the Persian kings are looted and set on fire.

events.title: Death of Darius
events.text: Darius III is murdered by his satrap Bessus as Alexander closes in.

events.title: Phrada
events.text: Philotas is tried and executed in Drangiana for an alleged plot.

events.title: Over the Hindu Kush
events.text: The army crosses the snowbound passes into Bactria in spring.

events.title: Alexandria Eschate
events.text: Alexander founds 'Alexandria the Furthest' on the Jaxartes.

events.title: Death of Cleitus
events.text: At Maracanda, Alexander kills his friend Cleitus in a drunken quarrel.

events.title: Marriage to Roxane
events.text: Alexander marries Roxane, daughter of the Bactrian noble Oxyartes.

events.title: Into India
events.text: From Alexandria in the Caucasus the army sets out for the Indus.

events.title: Swat valley
events.text: Alexander storms the towns of the Assacenians in the Swat valley.

events.title: Aornos
events.text: Alexander takes the rock of Aornos above the Indus, said to have defied Heracles.

events.title: Bridge of boats
events.text: Hephaestion bridges the Indus with boats; Taxiles welcomes the army.

events.title: Battle of the Hydaspes
events.text: Alexander crosses the river in a storm and defeats King Porus and his elephants.

events.title: Mutiny at the Hyphasis
events.text: The exhausted army refuses to march further east; Alexander turns back.

events.title: The fleet sets out
events.text: In November some 800 vessels, crewed by Phoenicians, Cypriots, Egyptians and Greeks, sail down the Hydaspes.

events.title: Rapids of the confluence
events.text: At the meeting of the Hydaspes and Acesines, whirlpools wreck several warships.

events.title: Wounded among the Malli
events.text: Storming a Malli town, Alexander is shot through the chest and nearly dies.

events.title: Patala
events.text: At the head of the Indus delta Alexander builds a harbour and docks.

events.title: Sacrifice to the Ocean
events.text: Alexander sails out into the open sea and pours libations to Poseidon.

events.title: Alexander's Harbour
events.text: Nearchus waits out the monsoon for weeks in a sheltered bay near today's Karachi.

events.title: Craterus' column
events.text: Craterus leads the veterans and elephants west through Arachosia.

events.title: Gedrosian desert
events.text: The army's sixty-day march through the desert costs thousands of lives.

events.title: Coast of the Fish-Eaters
events.text: The fleet, short of food, sails a barren coast whose people live on fish.

events.title: The whales
events.text: Sailors row at a school of spouting whales, blowing trumpets until they dive.

events.title: Reunion in Carmania
events.text: Near Harmozeia, Nearchus finds Alexander, who had feared the fleet lost.

events.title: Up the Pasitigris
events.text: The fleet reaches the head of the Gulf and rows upriver toward Susa.

events.title: Weddings at Susa
events.text: Nearchus is crowned with gold; Alexander and his officers marry Persian noblewomen.

events.title: Mutiny at Opis
events.text: Macedonian veterans mutiny on the Tigris before ten thousand are sent home.

events.title: Death of Hephaestion
events.text: Alexander's closest friend dies of fever at Ecbatana.

events.title: Ships carried overland
events.text: Phoenician warships are taken apart, hauled to Thapsacus and sail down to Babylon.

events.title: Sailors from Phoenicia
events.text: Agents with 500 talents hire seamen on the Phoenician and Syrian coast.

events.title: Babylon harbour
events.text: A harbour for a thousand warships and new docks are dug at Babylon.

events.title: Island of Icarus
events.text: Scouts reach Failaka at the head of the Gulf; Alexander names it Icarus.

events.title: Archias at Tylos
events.text: Archias sails a triaconter down the Gulf as far as Tylos, today's Bahrain.

events.title: Death of Alexander
events.text: On 10 or 11 June, days before the fleet was to sail for Arabia, Alexander dies in Babylon.

chartNote: Share of the area of eight present-day countries, from Cyprus to Pakistan, by their role in each year; regions are today's boundaries. Persian satrapies and Indian kingdoms had other borders, and a country's colour marks the main thing that happened there that year, a deliberate simplification. Dates follow Arrian and are approximate.
